title: Interfacial epitaxy of single-crystalline Al<sub>2</sub>(MoO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> flakes for anisotropic phonon polaritons
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74681-x

Metal molybdates exhibit interesting anisotropic thermal and mechanical properties, but the synthesis of single-crystalline films and the characterization of their light-matter interactions remain challenging. Here, the authors report the synthesis of single-crystalline Al2(MoO4)3 hosting hyperbolic phonon polaritons in the mid-infrared.

title: Hippocampo-neocortical interaction as compressive retrieval-augmented generation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74357-6

Here the authors model interactions between episodic and semantic memory as ‘retrieval-augmented generation’, explaining consolidation of structure from sequential experience, the reconstruction and distortion of memories, and their use in problem solving.

title: Magma convection favors ephemeral melt-rich bodies within mushy reservoirs
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74815-1

This study shows that magma convection greatly shortens the lifetime of mobilizable and eruptible magma at fast-spreading ridges to <2 years, highlighting the highly transient nature of magma bodies.

title: Solution-processed aqueous-insensitive transparent conductors for bio-optoelectronics
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74901-4

Long-term operation of bio-optoelectronics requires stable conductors for biological environments. Here, the authors develop a solution-processed transparent conductor that resists water-rich environments, enabling stable electrical recording and optical imaging on skin and brain surfaces.

title: Intrinsically nonlocal metamaterials
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74396-z

Electromagnetic nonlocality due to free electron motion is often associated with small corrections to the response of nanoscale conductive objects. Here the authors demonstrate that in metamaterials nonlocal interactions can quantitatively alter macroscale optical properties of the composites.

title: MIND: multimodal integration with neighbourhood-aware distributions
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74413-1

Multi-omics data integration is challenging due to missingness and inherent heterogeneity, current methods rely on assumptions that can cause information distortion. Here, the authors propose MIND, a platform that learns patient-specific embeddings from incomplete datasets.
